item.title: Haiku About an Autumn Road by Matsuo Bashō, in a New Translation
item.description: A haiku by Matsuo Bashō (1644–1694): This road — with no one walking on it, autumn dusk. A lonely road, and the courage to keep walking. Translation our own. From GLOBAL INNER DIVINE, a small studio in Japan.

item.title: Haiku About the Milky Way by Kobayashi Issa, in a New Translation
item.description: A haiku by Kobayashi Issa (1763–1828): How beautiful — through a hole in the paper screen, the Milky Way. Beauty, found through something broken. Translation our own. From GLOBAL INNER DIVINE, a small studio in Japan.

item.title: Haiku About Persimmons and a Temple Bell by Masaoka Shiki, in a New Translation
item.description: A haiku by Masaoka Shiki (1867–1902): I bite a persimmon — and a bell rings out at Hōryū-ji. Taste and sound, arriving together. Translation our own. From GLOBAL INNER DIVINE, a small studio in Japan.

item.title: Haiku About the Harvest Moon by Kobayashi Issa, in a New Translation
item.description: A haiku by Kobayashi Issa (1763–1828): “Get me that moon!” the child cries — the harvest moon. Some wishes are too beautiful to refuse, and too big to grant. Translation our own. From GLOBAL INNER DIVINE, a small studio in Japan.
